title: Self-Attention & Multiple Heads — Heads Share Capacity, Not Necessarily Work Evenly

body:
## Heads Share Capacity, Not Necessarily Work Evenly

Some heads learn sharp reusable patterns; others remain diffuse or redundant. More heads do not guarantee more independent reasoning.

Grouped-query attention shares key and value heads across several query heads. It reduces the key-value cache used during generation while retaining many query views.

Head pruning and interpretability plots are evidence tools, not proof of a complete explanation. Test the output change when a head is removed before assigning it a role.
common_mistakes: Every attention head is manually programmed with a grammar rule.
Self-attention compares a sequence only with an unrelated database.
Causal language models should train by looking at future answers.
